units.text: ⟦0⟧back-references⟦1⟧ are regular expression commands which refer to a previous part of the matched regular expression. Back-references are specified with backslash and a single digit (e.g. ‘⟦2⟧’). The part of the regular expression they refer to is called a ⟦3⟧subexpression⟦4⟧, and is designated with parentheses.
units.sourceHTML: back-references are regular expression commands which refer to a previous part of the matched regular expression. Back-references are specified with backslash and a single digit (e.g. ‘\1’). The part of the regular expression they refer to is called a subexpression, and is designated with parentheses.

units.text: Back-references and subexpressions are used in two cases: in the regular expression search pattern, and in the ⟦0⟧ part of the ⟦1⟧ command (see ⟦2⟧Regular Expression Addresses⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧The ⟦5⟧ Command⟦6⟧).
units.sourceHTML: Back-references and subexpressions are used in two cases: in the regular expression search pattern, and in the replacement part of the s command (see Regular Expression Addresses and The s Command).

units.text: In a regular expression pattern, back-references are used to match the same content as a previously matched subexpression. In the following example, the subexpression is ‘⟦0⟧’ - any single character (being surrounded by parentheses makes it a subexpression). The back-reference ‘⟦1⟧’ asks to match the same content (same character) as the sub-expression.
units.sourceHTML: In a regular expression pattern, back-references are used to match the same content as a previously matched subexpression. In the following example, the subexpression is ‘.’ - any single character (being surrounded by parentheses makes it a subexpression). The back-reference ‘\1’ asks to match the same content (same character) as the sub-expression.

units.text: When used with alternation, if the group does not participate in the match then the back-reference makes the whole match fail. For example, ‘⟦0⟧’ will not match ‘⟦1⟧’. When multiple regular expressions are given with ⟦2⟧ or from a file (‘⟦3⟧’), back-references are local to each expression.
units.sourceHTML: When used with alternation, if the group does not participate in the match then the back-reference makes the whole match fail. For example, ‘a(.)|b\1’ will not match ‘ba’. When multiple regular expressions are given with -e or from a file (‘-f file’), back-references are local to each expression.
